subject: Renewal kickoff — term options, capacity tradeoffs, and QBR scheduling
messages:
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Alice Sato <alice.sato@satsumahealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Apr 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal kickoff — term options, capacity tradeoffs, and QBR scheduling

Hi Alice and Satsuma team,

Thanks for the heads-up about the renewal window. I wanted to kick off the coordination so we can lock a plan before the end of May. High level goals: preserve latency SLOs for your surge windows, give you a predictable unit price, and keep an upgrade path if you want to scale later this year.

Proposed kickoff outcomes (actionable):
- Agree on term length (12 vs 24 months) and commit bands
- Pick QBR window to finalize the mutual action plan
- Confirm any procurement/legal milestones and who owns each item

Initial timeline (proposed)
- This week (Apr 29–May 3): confirm preferred term & QBR slots
- May 6–10: internal legal/finance review of draft terms
- May 13: Exec alignment and signoff target

Capacity tradeoffs to consider (short notes):
- Option A (Commit band): 100M tokens/month committed — lowest per-token unit cost, requires month-to-month smoothing for spikes
- Option B (Burst buffer): 70M tokens/month commit + 30M burst pool — slightly higher per-unit, reduces overprovisioning
- Option C (24-month staircase): stepped commit with built-in uplift credits for predictable growth

Attached is a short spreadsheet with modeled unit pricing across those options and a one-pager that maps SLAs to commit bands. Please review and tell me which two QBR slots work for your execs. I included a suggested May 7 or May 9 window — if neither works, propose alternatives and we'll adjust.

Next steps for us: once you confirm a slot I'll loop in legal and product for a 30-minute pre-QBR readout.

Attachments: satsuma_commit_options_2029-04-29.xlsx (pricing scenarios), renewal-summary-one-pager.pdf

Best,
Mateo Alvarez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
mateo.alvarez@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123
From: Alice Sato <alice.sato@satsumahealth.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@satsumahealth.com
Date: Mon, 29 Apr 2029 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal kickoff — term options, capacity tradeoffs, and QBR scheduling

Thanks Mateo — this is exactly what we needed to get started. Quick answers from our side:
- Term: leaning toward 12 months with an option to extend to 24 if the staircase pricing is attractive
- Capacity: we expect an average of ~60M tokens/month with monthly spikes up to ~110M across marketing bursts in Q3; burst pool looks useful

QBR availability (executive & procurement):
- Tue May 7, 10:00–10:45 PT (works for our CFO + Head of Product)
- Thu May 9, 14:00–14:45 PT (backup)

Can you include a simple scenario that shows: 12-month commit + 25% burst pool vs 24-month staircase with credits, and highlight the total invoice delta? Procurement also asked for a short list of what will be included in audit logs and retention for the committed tier.

Thanks — we can confirm the May 7 slot if you can send the updated scenarios + a doc brief on audit logs.

Best,
Alice Sato
Head of Platform Engineering, Satsuma Health
alice.sato@satsumahealth.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Apr 2029 12:15:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Renewal kickoff — internal (pricing posture & legal cadence)

Internal notes only — do not forward to customer.

DCI: DEAL-2029-0521 (Satsuma Health)

- Procurement asked for invoice delta scenarios; Mateo will send updated spreadsheet.
- Pricing posture recommendation: offer a 10% one-time commit credit if they sign a 12-month commit by May 20; if they choose 24-month staircase, propose 8% standard volume discount + 6% staged uplift credits.
- Legal checklist: standard T&Cs + data retention addendum (they specifically asked for audit log retention for 2 years). I will start a redline request with Legal and ask Kimberly to confirm SLA language for surge support.

Ben — can you prep an ops note on how the burst pool is enforced (soft vs hard throttles) and include expected latency behavior at 100–120M token spikes? Kimberly — plan to route a first pass redline to Satsuma legal on May 3 so procurement has time for internal review.

Thanks,
Marissa
VP, Renewal & Expansion, Redwood Inference
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Alice Sato <alice.sato@satsumahealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Apr 2029 14:30:00 -0700
Subject: Confirming May 7 QBR + updated scenarios attached

Alice — thanks for the quick reply. May 7, 10:00–10:45 PT works for our execs and procurement — I’ve tentatively blocked that slot on the calendar (see link below). We’ve attached two clean scenarios as requested:

1) 12-month commit + 25% burst pool (sheet: 12m_commit_plus_burst) — shows invoice delta and expected overage exposure
2) 24-month staircase with uplift credits (sheet: 24m_staircase_credit) — shows blended per-token price and credit schedule

I also attached a short audit-log brief that lists retention and types of events included for the committed tier.

Next steps:
- May 1: internal legal sends first-pass redline to Satsuma (Marissa/Kimberly owner)
- May 7: QBR (40 min) — finalize mutual action plan and signpost final term by May 13
- May 13: target signoff and PO submission

Links & attachments:
- HubSpot deal: https://hubspot.redwood.com/deal/DEAL-2029-0521
- Calendar (tentative): https://calendar.google.com/event?eid=May7-10am-PT-QBR
- Attachments: satsuma_commit_options_2029-04-29.xlsx, renewal-summary-one-pager.pdf

If procurement needs any additional compliance artifacts (SOC2 scope, data retention cert) ahead of the legal review, call that out and we’ll prioritize.

See you on May 7,
Mateo Alvarez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
mateo.alvarez@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123
